The documents contain pricing and availability for requested items but do not indicate a confirmed order. You'll be provided with OCR-extracted text and one or more attachments belonging to the SAME supplier email. The email body and the attachments together MAY contain MULTIPLE distinct quotations (for example, one quotation per attached PDF, or several quotations clearly separated within a single document/email).

Today's Date in ISO format:
2026-06-25T08:19:51.248049+00:00

**Your task:**
- Identify EVERY distinct quotation present in the combined payload (email body + attachments).
- Priortise the data recieved from pdf , if not then excel and then email body.
- No duplication of data, if same part numbers are mentiend with same qty and price, properly deduplicate that 
- Different attachment may contain same quotation
- If same quotation is present in multiple attachments, then combine the data from all the attachments and return a single quotation object.
- For each distinct quotation, extract the full set of fields described in the per-quotation schema below.
- Return a single top-level JSON object with the key ``quotations`` whose value is a JSON array. Each element of the array is one fully-populated quotation object using the schema below. If only one quotation is present, return an array with a single element. If no quotation can be extracted, return ``{"quotations": []}``.

**How to decide what counts as a distinct quotation:**
- A unique ``quote_number`` almost always indicates a distinct quotation. Different ``quote_number`` values MUST become separate elements in the ``quotations`` array.
- Different attachments that each look like a complete standalone quotation (their own header, supplier block, line items, totals) MUST become separate elements even if the ``quote_number`` is missing.
- Do NOT split a single quotation into multiple elements just because its line items span multiple pages or sheets.
- Do NOT merge two clearly distinct quotations (different quote numbers, different RFQs, or different supplier reference numbers) into one element.

**Per-quotation schema (each element of ``quotations`` must follow this exact shape):**
```json
{
  "quote_number": "This is supplier’s provided quotation number. Find and extract the quotation number from the text. It may appear as quote number, quotation number, quote no, quote ref, or it can appear as simple heading as string",
  "rfq_number": "This is the Request for Quotation (RFQ) number. Find and extract the RFQ number from the text. It may appear as RFQ number, RFQ no, RFQ#, enquiry number ,requisition no or similar as string",
  "quote_date": "The date when the quotation was issued, in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) as string",
  "quote_expiry_date": "The expiration date of the quotation, in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) as string",
  "shipping_and_delivery": {
    "shipping_instructions": {
      "delivery_method": "The delivery method mentioned, e.g., standard, express, courier as string",
      "special_handling": "Any special handling instructions such as fragile, temperature-controlled, hazardous as string",
      "insurance": "Whether insurance is required/optional/none as stated in the quotation as string"
    },
    "shipping_method": "The primary shipping method used, e.g., Air, Sea, Road, Courier. Mandatory field as string",
    "delivery_location": "The final delivery location or warehouse specified in the quotation as string",
    "bill_to_address": {
      "street": "Street portion of the consignee's address as string",
      "city": "City of consignee's address as string",
      "state": "State/Province/Region of consignee's address as string",
      "zipcode": "Postal code as string",
      "country": "3-letter ISO ALPHA-3 country code, e.g., IND for India"
    },
    "ship_to_address": {
      "street": "Street portion of the consignee's address as string",
      "city": "City of consignee's address as string",
      "state": "State/Province/Region of consignee's address as string",
      "zipcode": "Postal code as string",
      "country": "3-letter ISO ALPHA-3 country code, e.g., IND for India as string"
    }
  },
  "supplier_information": {
    "supplier_name": "The name of the supplier issuing the quotation as string",
    "supplier_email": "email of supplier in the document else none as string"
    "address": "The supplier's full address in a single line as string",
    "contact": "Primary phone number of supplier contact person, if provided as string",
    "website": "Supplier's website URL, if available as string"
  },
  "currency": "The currency used in the quotation as ISO 4217 code, e.g., USD as string",
  "notes": [
    "General notes from the quotation, such as 'IN STOCK', 'Pricing does not include freight', etc. Include each note as a separate string in this list, Discount mentioned on total price. as list of string"
  ],
  "payment_terms": "[Terms and condition decided for payment between buyer and supplier]",
  "certifications_required": "[Document-level certifications. Use standard names: ISO 9001, ISO 14001, RoHS, REACH, CE, UL, CSA, AS9100, IATF 16949, FDA, etc. Normalize variants (e.g. 'CE Mark'→CE, 'RoHS Compliant'→RoHS). As list of strings; use null or [] if none.]",
  "incoterms": "[One of the 11 ICC Incoterms® 2020 rules only: EXW, FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DPU, DDP, FAS, FOB, CFR, CIF. Extract the code only (e.g. 'FOB' from 'FOB Singapore'). Map common phrases to the standard code (e.g. 'Delivered Duty Paid'→DDP, 'Free on Board'→FOB). If no valid Incoterm is found, use null.]",
  "buyer": {
    "name": "Name of the consignee company receiving the goods, must be $consignee_company as string",
    "address": {
      "street": "Street portion of the consignee's address as string",
      "city": "City of consignee's address as string",
      "state": "State/Province/Region of consignee's address as string",
      "zipcode": "Postal code as string",
      "country": "3-letter ISO ALPHA-3 country code, e.g., IND for India"
    },
    "contact_person": "Buyer-side contact name if specified as string"
  },
  "line_items": [
    {
      "part_number": "Identify the part number or uniquely identifiable string; e.g. item_code, SKU, model_number. Do not create on your own. If none available, default to description. as string",
      "manufacturer_part_number": "Extract manufacturer part number from 'PART:', 'MFG P/N:', or next to manufacturer name. Do not create on your own. If none available, default to description. as string",
      "description": "Item or product description. as string",
      "reach_status": "Compliance status with REACH regulation, e.g., 'UNAFFECTED' as string",
      "quantity": <Order quantity of item. as int>,
      "unit_price": <Unit-level price of the item as float, round off to 5 decimal points or the nearest 5 decimal points>,
      "total_price": <Total (extended) line item price as float, round off to 5 decimal points or the nearest 5 decimal points>,
      "status": "Status of this part number: ACTIVE if sender is quoting with details else UNABLE_TO_QUOTE as string",
      "reason": "If status is UNABLE_TO_QUOTE reason if stated. as string",
      "moq": <Minimum Order Quantity for this part. as int>,
      "differential_pricing": [
        {
          "quantity": <Minimum quantity for this pricing tier as int>,
          "unit_price": <Unit price at this quantity tier as float, round off to 5 decimal points or the nearest 5 decimal points>,
          "lead_time":{
                      "duration": "duration of lead time mentioned for this diff pricing for ex: 7-8 weeks as 7-8 and 8 days as 8 as string "
                      "lead_time_unit":"Unit of lead time for this diff pricing such as days/weeks/month"
                      }
        }
      ],
      "country_of_origin": "country of origin of line item",
      "mfg_lead_time_weeks": <Manufacturing lead time in weeks, as an int>,
      "delivery_date": "delivery date for the mentioned for line item in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) as string"
      "notes": "[Any additional comments specific to the line item as list of str, such as Discount mentioned on this part]",
      "certifications": "[Certifications for this line item. Use standard names: ISO 9001, RoHS, REACH, CE, UL, CSA, etc. Normalize variants to standard abbreviations. As list of strings; use null or [] if none.]",
      "metadata": {
        "discount": <Discount offered on this part as float i.e if its 8.5% then 8.5 as int>
        }
    },
  ],
  "total_amount": <Total of all line item prices combined, as a float>,
  "status": "if supplier is not quoting populate this field as UNABLE_TO_QUOTE other wise ACTIVE as string",
  "reason": "Populate reason why supplier is not quoting as string",
  "metadata": {}
}
```

**Top-level response shape (MUST follow exactly):**
```json
{
  "quotations": [
    { /* per-quotation schema element #1 */ },
    { /* per-quotation schema element #2 */ }
  ]
}
```

**Instructions for Extraction Vision**
- The combined payload may include the email body and one or more attachments belonging to the same email. Treat the email body as supporting context that may add or clarify fields for any of the quotations (for example payment terms, supplier email, expiry, currency).
- You should always create lineitems for each partnumber with proper status unless no partnumber is mentioned
- Ensure the unit price is calculated correctly. For example, if the price is $4000 for 100 units, the unit price should be recorded as $40 per unit. Always convert bulk pricing into a per-unit price before populating the field
- If supplier is denying for quoting and no part number is mentioned then means it is for all partnumber then dont create any lineitems keep the array empty
- Don't confuse MOQ (Minimum Order Quantity) with multiple line items — those should fall under differential_pricing
- For each part number, there should be only one line item, except in cases where separate line items are clearly specified and not related to MOQ
- Present the results in the form of a detailed and valid JSON response that adheres to the template guidelines, without code blocks or any extra text.
- If the supplier mentions that an item is “in stock” or “available now,” the lead time should be set to zero at both levels, based on the specified data type
- Analyzes the input dates to determine the most likely format used.
- **Dates**: All date fields (quote_date, quote_expiry_date, delivery_date, etc.) must be in ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DD. Convert any other date format to YYYY-MM-DD.
- For dates (if applicable): Use Today's Date ISO format above with date-like strings in the document to resolve ambiguous day/month order where needed.
- When extracting an RFQ or Quote number, do not add prefixes like "RFQ" or "Quote" unless they are explicitly present in the source text (e.g., "RFQ: rfq 2412" or "Quote: quot 21412"). Extract the number exactly as written unless the prefix is clearly specified.
$use_american_date_format
- Ensure that each line item in the "line_items" array represents a physical product or good, and not a service/service charges/labour/labour charges/charges/taxes/fees/shipping charges/transportation charges/warranties/insurance or any other non-physical items.
- **Differential Pricing**: Only populate the "differential_pricing" array if the quotation explicitly provides volume-based pricing tiers (e.g., "1-10 units: $50/unit, 11-50 units: $45/unit, 51+ units: $40/unit"). If no differential pricing is mentioned, use `null` for this field. The differential_pricing array should be sorted by quantity in ascending order.
- If certain information is not mentioned or is unclear, use `null` JSON literal or appropriate placeholders as per the template guidelines.
- Fill in the template accurately, adhering to the specified data types and values.
- Always wrap your output in the top-level ``{"quotations": [...]}`` shape, even when only one quotation is present.
- **Price Precision**: All `unit_price` fields (both in `line_items` and `differential_pricing`) and `total_price` must be a float rounded to 5 decimal points or the nearest 5 decimal points. If the value terminates before 5 decimal places, use the exact value (e.g. 40.0, 12.5). Never truncate — always apply standard rounding for the 5th decimal digit.

input.content:
You are an expert in extracting details from supplier-generated quotation documents, typically created by a seller or distributor and shared with a buyer. The documents contain pricing and availability for requested items but do not indicate a confirmed order. You'll be provided with OCR-extracted text and one or more attachments belonging to the SAME supplier email. The email body and the attachments together MAY contain MULTIPLE distinct quotations (for example, one quotation per attached PDF, or several quotations clearly separated within a single document/email).

Today's Date in ISO format:
2026-09-03T10:33:27.080077+00:00

**Your task:**
- Identify EVERY distinct quotation present in the combined payload (email body + attachments).
- Priortise the data recieved from pdf , if not then excel and then email body.
- No duplication of data, if same part numbers are mentiend with same qty and price, properly deduplicate that 
- Different attachment may contain same quotation
- If same quotation is present in multiple attachments, then combine the data from all the attachments and return a single quotation object.
- For each distinct quotation, extract the full set of fields described in the per-quotation schema below.
- Return a single top-level JSON object with the key ``quotations`` whose value is a JSON array. Each element of the array is one fully-populated quotation object using the schema below. If only one quotation is present, return an array with a single element. If no quotation can be extracted, return ``{"quotations": []}``.

**How to decide what counts as a distinct quotation:**
- A unique ``quote_number`` almost always indicates a distinct quotation. Different ``quote_number`` values MUST become separate elements in the ``quotations`` array.
- Different attachments that each look like a complete standalone quotation (their own header, supplier block, line items, totals) MUST become separate elements even if the ``quote_number`` is missing.
- Do NOT split a single quotation into multiple elements just because its line items span multiple pages or sheets.
- Do NOT merge two clearly distinct quotations (different quote numbers, different RFQs, or different supplier reference numbers) into one element.

**Per-quotation schema (each element of ``quotations`` must follow this exact shape):**
```json
{
  "quote_number": "This is supplier’s provided quotation number. Find and extract the quotation number from the text. It may appear as quote number, quotation number, quote no, quote ref, or it can appear as simple heading as string",
  "rfq_number": "This is the Request for Quotation (RFQ) number. Find and extract the RFQ number from the text. It may appear as RFQ number, RFQ no, RFQ#, enquiry number ,requisition no or similar as string",
  "quote_date": "The date when the quotation was issued, in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) as string",
  "quote_expiry_date": "The expiration date of the quotation, in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) as string",
  "shipping_and_delivery": {
    "shipping_instructions": {
      "delivery_method": "The delivery method mentioned, e.g., standard, express, courier as string",
      "special_handling": "Any special handling instructions such as fragile, temperature-controlled, hazardous as string",
      "insurance": "Whether insurance is required/optional/none as stated in the quotation as string"
    },
    "shipping_method": "The primary shipping method used, e.g., Air, Sea, Road, Courier. Mandatory field as string",
    "delivery_location": "The final delivery location or warehouse specified in the quotation as string",
    "bill_to_address": {
      "street": "Street portion of the consignee's address as string",
      "city": "City of consignee's address as string",
      "state": "State/Province/Region of consignee's address as string",
      "zipcode": "Postal code as string",
      "country": "3-letter ISO ALPHA-3 country code, e.g., IND for India"
    },
    "ship_to_address": {
      "street": "Street portion of the consignee's address as string",
      "city": "City of consignee's address as string",
      "state": "State/Province/Region of consignee's address as string",
      "zipcode": "Postal code as string",
      "country": "3-letter ISO ALPHA-3 country code, e.g., IND for India as string"
    }
  },
  "supplier_information": {
    "supplier_name": "The name of the supplier issuing the quotation as string",
    "supplier_email": "email of supplier in the document else none as string"
    "address": "The supplier's full address in a single line as string",
    "contact": "Primary phone number of supplier contact person, if provided as string",
    "website": "Supplier's website URL, if available as string"
  },
  "currency": "The currency used in the quotation as ISO 4217 code, e.g., USD as string",
  "notes": [
    "General notes from the quotation, such as 'IN STOCK', 'Pricing does not include freight', etc. Include each note as a separate string in this list, Discount mentioned on total price. as list of string"
  ],
  "payment_terms": "[Terms and condition decided for payment between buyer and supplier]",
  "certifications_required": "[Document-level certifications. Use standard names: ISO 9001, ISO 14001, RoHS, REACH, CE, UL, CSA, AS9100, IATF 16949, FDA, etc. Normalize variants (e.g. 'CE Mark'→CE, 'RoHS Compliant'→RoHS). As list of strings; use null or [] if none.]",
  "incoterms": "[One of the 11 ICC Incoterms® 2020 rules only: EXW, FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DPU, DDP, FAS, FOB, CFR, CIF. Extract the code only (e.g. 'FOB' from 'FOB Singapore'). Map common phrases to the standard code (e.g. 'Delivered Duty Paid'→DDP, 'Free on Board'→FOB). If no valid Incoterm is found, use null.]",
  "buyer": {
    "name": "Name of the consignee company receiving the goods, must be $consignee_company as string",
    "address": {
      "street": "Street portion of the consignee's address as string",
      "city": "City of consignee's address as string",
      "state": "State/Province/Region of consignee's address as string",
      "zipcode": "Postal code as string",
      "country": "3-letter ISO ALPHA-3 country code, e.g., IND for India"
    },
    "contact_person": "Buyer-side contact name if specified as string"
  },
  "line_items": [
    {
      "part_number": "Identify the part number or uniquely identifiable string; e.g. item_code, SKU, model_number. Do not create on your own. If none available, default to description. as string",
      "manufacturer_part_number": "Extract manufacturer part number from 'PART:', 'MFG P/N:', or next to manufacturer name. Do not create on your own. If none available, default to description. as string",
      "description": "Item or product description. as string",
      "reach_status": "Compliance status with REACH regulation, e.g., 'UNAFFECTED' as string",
      "quantity": <Order quantity of item. as int>,
      "unit_price": <Unit-level price of the item as float, round off to 5 decimal points or the nearest 5 decimal points>,
      "total_price": <Total (extended) line item price as float, round off to 5 decimal points or the nearest 5 decimal points>,
      "status": "Status of this part number: ACTIVE if sender is quoting with details else UNABLE_TO_QUOTE as string",
      "reason": "If status is UNABLE_TO_QUOTE reason if stated. as string",
      "moq": <Minimum Order Quantity for this part. as int>,
      "differential_pricing": [
        {
          "quantity": <Minimum quantity for this pricing tier as int>,
          "unit_price": <Unit price at this quantity tier as float, round off to 5 decimal points or the nearest 5 decimal points>,
          "lead_time":{
                      "duration": "duration of lead time mentioned for this diff pricing for ex: 7-8 weeks as 7-8 and 8 days as 8 as string "
                      "lead_time_unit":"Unit of lead time for this diff pricing such as days/weeks/month"
                      }
        }
      ],
      "country_of_origin": "country of origin of line item",
      "mfg_lead_time_weeks": <Manufacturing lead time in weeks, as an int>,
      "delivery_date": "delivery date for the mentioned for line item in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) as string"
      "notes": "[Any additional comments specific to the line item as list of str, such as Discount mentioned on this part]",
      "certifications": "[Certifications for this line item. Use standard names: ISO 9001, RoHS, REACH, CE, UL, CSA, etc. Normalize variants to standard abbreviations. As list of strings; use null or [] if none.]",
      "metadata": {
        "discount": <Discount offered on this part as float i.e if its 8.5% then 8.5 as int>
        }
    },
  ],
  "total_amount": <Total of all line item prices combined, as a float>,
  "status": "if supplier is not quoting populate this field as UNABLE_TO_QUOTE other wise ACTIVE as string",
  "reason": "Populate reason why supplier is not quoting as string",
  "metadata": {}
}
```

**Top-level response shape (MUST follow exactly):**
```json
{
  "quotations": [
    { /* per-quotation schema element #1 */ },
    { /* per-quotation schema element #2 */ }
  ]
}
```

**Instructions for Extraction Vision**
- The combined payload may include the email body and one or more attachments belonging to the same email. Treat the email body as supporting context that may add or clarify fields for any of the quotations (for example payment terms, supplier email, expiry, currency).
- You should always create lineitems for each partnumber with proper status unless no partnumber is mentioned
- Ensure the unit price is calculated correctly. For example, if the price is $4000 for 100 units, the unit price should be recorded as $40 per unit. Always convert bulk pricing into a per-unit price before populating the field
- If supplier is denying for quoting and no part number is mentioned then means it is for all partnumber then dont create any lineitems keep the array empty
- Don't confuse MOQ (Minimum Order Quantity) with multiple line items — those should fall under differential_pricing
